# Published experimental router check matrix

This is a tests-only source qualification campaign for issue #10577. The provider
is the actual published `vue-router@5.4.0` archive, with its npm integrity,
complete provider-file custody, and immutable dependency lock. Its real scanner
produces the complete declarations, route module and resolver module. The checker
host is independently locked to `typescript@7.1.0-dev.20261017.1`.

The strict Vue TS matrix covers LF and CRLF, a valid program, thirteen independent
invalid mutations, and repair. The mutations include required, optional and
repeated paths; required, defaulted, array and custom Date query parameters; hash
parameters; `push`, `replace`, `resolve`, and a `RouterLink` target. The valid
program also instantiates `RouterView`. Generated native code is retained whole;
the repaired complete native packet must equal the original valid packet.

The native process oracle is the separately locked, already published
`vize@0.562.0` archive running with the exact same pinned 7.1 checker backend and
authored project. Compare the complete unmodified JSON stdout, status, signal,
error and stderr; no diagnostic, program, message or version field is omitted.
Executable identity and process timing remain separately retained metadata.
Pinned 5.9 SFC diagnostic packets and fresh plain TS programs are independent
reference witnesses. For the invalid `resolve` overload, 5.9 reports the callee
while 7.1 reports the object argument; preserve both actual ranges literally.
This distinction does not confer full cross-backend diagnostic range parity.
No union normalization or candidate-generated expected messages are used.

Executable scanner modules embed absolute imports. Their sole root transport is
an authority roster of eleven UTF8 spans: five dynamic page imports in each
module and one static parser import in the resolver. The pinned 5.9 AST must
prove every span's StringLiteral role and decoded old-root value. Only those
expected import values move to the admitted runner root; all remaining bytes are
exact. Original, transported and actual modules and hashes remain artifacts.
Wrong boundaries, foreign roots, extra/missing imports, changed literals,
members and text are negative controls. Complete scanner outputs use lossless
JSON storage to retain their original final blank lines.

Every actual process records its command, arguments, status, signal, error,
stdout, stderr and elapsed time before assertions. This preserves the complete
native report and generated code, the pinned SFC reference, independent plain TS
targets, the scanner output, dependency identities and source executable custody.
Timing records measure these individual processes, not a production speed claim.

The separate format probe artifact is discovery evidence. It executes invalid
and repaired JS SFC, standalone TS and TSX, `.art.vue`, Pug and Jade inputs.
Standalone TS/TSX use an explicit named route rather than a file-inferred page.
The independent reference lacks adapters for Art variant templates and Pug/Jade
templates; their script results cannot confer template equivalence. Those
limitations and complete process packets remain visible. Discovery-only probes
do not establish universal format, LSP, editor or content-mapper support.
